1.explanation: To support selective decluttering (for example only text or only images) the style classes need a new ignorePlacement option, but Image.js and Text.js don’t yet declare or carry that flag through. The canvas builders (ImageBuilder.js and TextBuilder.js) read style properties and assemble draw instructions—because ignorePlacement isn’t passed down, the executor can’t honor it and falls back to hiding or mis-ordering features whenever declutterMode≠'declutter'. Adding ignorePlacement support to the style constructors/getters/setters and having the builders pull style.getIgnorePlacement() into their instruction arrays fixes placement behavior for non-declutter modes.
1.bug_scenario: The issue manifests when you draw point features with both an icon and a text label while using declutterMode values other than the default “declutter” (for example “obstacle” or “none”). In that case icons and labels either overlap incorrectly or one element disappears. In the reference screenshots you’ll see markers and labels that should never collide nevertheless being hidden or drawn at the wrong Z-order when declutterMode is “obstacle”/“none”.
